extracted.intended_audience: research software authors submitting to JOSS; JOSS contributors and community members (including reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and community standards for submitting research software papers to the Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS), and for interacting in the JOSS community (including review interactions). Covers the target work, submission expectations, and behavioral rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target: research software packages
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS) is a developer friendly journal for research software packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be about research software; JOSS exists to provide an academic venue for software so it can be cited. Papers about software are the appropriate output for academic credit in this venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review goal: improve submitted software quality
rubrics_metrics.description: JOSS is an academic journal with a formal peer review process that is designed to improve the quality of the software submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and the review process should focus on actions that improve the software itself (bug fixes, documentation, usability, correctness), not just assess novelty. Reviewers should provide feedback that leads to measurable improvements in the software package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developer-friendly submission: simple workflow and documentation expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: JOSS provides a simple submission workflow and extensive documentation to help prepare submissions; if the software is already well documented then paper preparation should take no more than an hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to have well-documented software (installation instructions, usage examples, API docs) so that preparing the short JOSS paper is quick. Lack of adequate documentation is an anti-pattern because it increases the effort required to prepare a paper and for reviewers to evaluate the software.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: All interactions in the JOSS community must adhere to the Code of Conduct adapted from the Contributor Covenant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code of Conduct is strictly enforced across official JOSS repositories, the JOSS website, and resources. If someone violates the terms, report to the Editor-in-Chief or the editorial board. This is a required community standard that governs reviewer-author and contributor interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of JOSS platforms and review workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are handled via the JOSS submission tool (https://joss.theoj.org) and reviews are managed in the JOSS reviews repository (https://github.com/openjournals/joss-reviews/issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers should follow the established submission and review channels (the submission tool and the reviews repo). Procedural correctness (submitting through the proper tool and participating in the reviews repository) is required for a valid submission/review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance outcome: DOI and listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance into JOSS, a CrossRef DOI is minted and the paper is listed on the JOSS website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware that acceptance yields a citable DOI and public listing; this clarifies the journal's purpose of providing academic credit for software. This is an expected outcome rather than a submission criterion, but informs authors' motivations and expectations.
